packageRules.groupName: GitHub Actions minor and patch updates
packageRules.description: GitHub Actions' minor and patch updates in one pull request (the actions only: the CI jobs' python-version and node-version and any docker:// image stay on their own)
init, analyze and upload-sarif must share one version: analyze refuses a configuration written by a different init
The web UI's development tools: one pull request for their minor and patch updates
react and react-dom must have the exact same version, and the type packages follow them. After frontend-dev, so the type packages land here: the last matching rule wins
@types/node describes the Node.js release the app is built and tested with; its major version moves with that by hand, not on its own
ansible-core 2.20 supports Python 3.12 to 3.14 on the control node: the image and CI stay below 3.15 until ansible-core moves too
The image runs ansible-core 2.20 (requirements.txt caps it below 2.21); a newer line is tested and moved by hand, together with the Python it supports
Node.js long-term-support releases only (even numbers); odd releases reach end of life within months
The test target image has one stage per Ubuntu LTS release: only the digests move, never the release
The same for the test target image's other stages (one per Rocky Linux and AlmaLinux release)
The project's own image, published by the release workflow
Dependabot's auto-merge workflow is the only user of dependabot/fetch-metadata and stays idle now: Renovate leaves its pin alone
The test target image is checked daily, as Dependabot did: quay.io deletes the digest a CentOS Stream tag left within days

Patch and minor updates of the Python and npm packages and the GitHub Actions merge by themselves (squash, once every required check passes) after a 3-day wait. Security fixes skip the wait (Renovate's vulnerabilityAlerts default) and merge the same way only if they are patch or minor. Majors and updates without a version level never match
Never by themselves: Docker image updates of any kind, including docker:// and container images named in workflows
The CI jobs' interpreter versions (python-version, node-version) wait for the maintainer: they move the interpreter the checks run on

The one image exception: the CentOS Stream digests of the test target image merge by themselves with no wait, because quay.io deletes the digest a tag left within days and the integration tests break while the update waits. Digest updates only; a move to another tag still waits for the maintainer

requirements.txt and requirements-dev.txt are included (-r) by the two pip-compile inputs, so pip-compile sees their packages as indirect dependencies of the lock files, which Renovate turns off by default. Turn them on: every pin in requirements-ci.txt and requirements-webui.txt may move (the .in files and the hand-set floors never change)

requirements-fuzz.txt pins atheris by hash, and a pin edit there needs its hashes rewritten with hashin, which would also add hashes for files the pin leaves out on purpose (only the Linux x86-64 wheels): so the maintainer reviews it
